site.name: runeforge-docs
site.summary: runeforge-docs Fictional state-management JavaScript library "Runeforge" official documentation site (Redux / Zustand-style ergonomics). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Sticky topbar with brand+version pill, doc tabs, ⌘K search trigger, version selector, theme toggle, GitHub stars; **three-column layout**: left categorized TOC tree (5 sections, 26 items), center page with hero / install code-tabs (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun) / "Hello, store" code-tabs (5 framework adapters: Vanilla / React / Solid / Svelte 5 / Vue 3) with copy button / 3-tile "three things to remember" / 6-row why-table comparing to Redux / Zustand / Jotai / next-steps list / prev/next pager; right-side on-this-page TOC. - `guide-quickstart.html` — 5-minute tutorial. Step-by-step build of a counter store, todo list with derived store, async fetcher with `asyncSlice()`, and devtools install. Lots of code blocks and an info / success callout. - `guide-stores.html` — Stores reference. Store API table; reading + subscribing; immutability warning callout; composing with `derive()`; slicing with `store.select()`; SSR (`toJSON` / `fromJSON`); testing pattern. - `guide-actions.html` — Actions & selectors. Action rules; selector c

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the Runeforge docs site as a documentation/product UX, with emphasis on the primary getting-started path and the adjacent reference/example paths that a new user would use to evaluate and adopt the library.
run_plan.summary: Start on the docs home page and validate the main onboarding path: introduction, install instructions, hello-store examples, and navigation to the quickstart. Then cover the core concept pages and the API reference to confirm the docs hierarchy, in-page navigation, and content depth are coherent. Finish by checking examples and key mobile behaviors, with special attention to controls that are already flagged as small or unlabeled in the prescan.
assumptions: The main exploration flow is documentation-led rather than a transactional checkout flow, so success means clear discoverability, navigation, and comprehension across docs pages.

The visible top-level links are the authoritative site map for the run; items shown as '#' may be placeholders or non-functional and should be treated as lower-confidence adjacency, not guaranteed destinations.
The site should remain usable without console/network errors; the main validation focus is content structure, control behavior, and responsive ergonomics.
Search, version switching, theme toggle, and copy buttons are expected to be interactive even though only some are explicitly shown in the prescan.
risk_hotspots: Top-bar controls on index.html: Search docs ⌘K, version select, theme toggle, and GitHub/star link are small tap targets on mobile and include an unlabeled select in the prescan.
Left navigation / docs tree on index.html: several entries are placeholder '#' links, so verify which items navigate and whether the active state is clear.
Code-tab switches and copy buttons on index.html, guide-quickstart.html, and examples.html: important for reading/install flows and likely to be error-prone on mobile.
guide-quickstart.html: dense step-by-step tutorial with multiple code blocks and callouts; verify that progression through install/counter/todo/async/devtools remains readable and scannable.
guide-stores.html and guide-actions.html: concept-heavy pages with tables and code examples; confirm anchors, headings, and explanatory structure are easy to traverse.
api-reference.html: the longest reference page and likely to have the heaviest in-page TOC/anchor interaction; validate symbol discoverability and section navigation.
examples.html: filter input, category chips, and example cards are primary interactive controls; inspect whether filtering is understandable and mobile-friendly.

phases.title: Home page orientation
phases.objective: Validate the docs landing page as the entry point, including primary navigation, versioning, theme toggle, search trigger, and the three-column docs layout.
key_checks: Open the docs home and confirm the left TOC, center content, and right on-this-page TOC all feel clearly related.
Check the top-bar controls: Docs/API/Examples navigation, Search docs ⌘K, version selector, theme toggle, and GitHub/star affordance.
Exercise the install code tabs and the hello-store framework tabs to ensure tab state changes visibly and the copy button is available.
Verify the page provides clear next-step paths into Quickstart, Stores, Actions & selectors, and API reference.
exit_criteria: All visible primary navigation groups have been visited or tested.
At least one code-tab set and one copy interaction have been validated.
No obvious broken or confusing entry-point behavior remains unobserved.

phases.title: Quickstart onboarding flow
phases.objective: Validate the 5-minute tutorial as the canonical new-user path from install to first app patterns.
key_checks: Confirm the step structure from install through counter, todo list, async fetcher, and devtools is legible and sequential.
Test any in-page anchors/TOC links for jumping between sections.
Inspect code block readability and any copy controls or code-tab behavior present on the page.
Check that the success/info callouts support the tutorial narrative rather than interrupt it.
exit_criteria: Each major quickstart step has been reviewed at least once.
The page supports easy progression from one tutorial section to the next.
Key code examples are readable without layout collapse.

phases.title: Core concepts depth check
phases.objective: Validate the conceptual docs that explain how stores, actions, and selectors work together, including composition and subscriptions.
key_checks: Review the stores reference for creation, subscribing, composing, slicing, SSR/serialization, and testing sections.
Review the actions/selectors page for selector rules, composition, reusable action creators, and middleware guidance.
Check whether tables, callouts, and example blocks are easy to parse and whether anchor navigation matches the headings.
Verify cross-links back to the main docs and adjacent pages are understandable.
exit_criteria: Both core-concept pages have been traversed through their main sections.
The docs hierarchy from stores to actions/selectors is understandable.
No missing-content or broken-anchor issues are left untested for these pages.

phases.title: Reference and symbol lookup
phases.objective: Validate the API reference as a deep lookup page for public symbols, adapter utilities, and errors.
key_checks: Confirm the API reference overview and major function sections are reachable via the page TOC.
Inspect key symbols such as forge(), derive(), use(), asyncSlice(), listSlice(), formSlice(), and devtools().
Check the React adapter section and any re-export or error documentation at the bottom.
Assess whether the reference page is scannable enough for experienced users looking for exact API details.
exit_criteria: The top-level symbol categories and at least several major entries have been visited.
Anchor/TOC navigation works as expected across the reference page.
The page supports efficient lookup without obvious structural confusion.

phases.title: Examples discovery and filtering
phases.objective: Validate the examples gallery as a discovery surface for practical patterns and learning by imitation.
key_checks: Test the example filter input and category chips (All, Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, SSR).
Review representative examples across levels, including counter, todo persistence, async fetcher, and a more advanced pattern.
Check whether example summaries communicate framework, LOC, and complexity clearly.
Verify filtering and browsing remain usable when moving through different categories.
exit_criteria: Filtering controls have been exercised and at least a few example cards have been reviewed.
The page clearly supports both beginner and advanced discovery paths.
The examples grid remains readable and navigable.

phases.title: Responsive and control validation
phases.objective: Repeat the most important interactions in a mobile viewport and specifically probe the small or unlabeled controls called out by the prescan.
key_checks: Re-check the top bar on mobile for tap-target usability, including Search docs ⌘K, version selector, theme toggle, and star/GitHub affordances.
Verify the left navigation, code tabs, copy buttons, and example filters remain usable without accidental taps.
Confirm the unlabeled select on the home/reference pages is still operable and its purpose is inferable.
Look for truncated content, overlapping columns, or anchor/TOC issues when the layout stacks.
exit_criteria: Critical controls from the main flow have been re-tested on mobile.
The pages remain navigable in a narrow viewport without major layout breakage.
Any mobile-only friction points are recorded against the specific control or page.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages: index.html, guide-quickstart.html, guide-stores.html, guide-actions.html, api-reference.html, and examples.html.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the primary nav, left TOC, on-page anchors, code tabs, copy buttons, filter controls, and representative reference symbol links on each major page.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the homepage, quickstart, reference, and examples interactions on mobile viewport, with extra scrutiny on small tap targets and the unlabeled select.

notes: Treat placeholder '#' links as validation targets for affordance quality and consistency, not as guaranteed destinations.
Prioritize breadth first, then deeper inspection of dense pages and controls with known accessibility warnings.
Because the prescan shows no console or network errors, focus on UX issues, content clarity, and responsive interaction quality rather than failure recovery paths.

Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Core concepts › Stores Core concept Stores. A store is the unit of state in Runeforge. It owns a single piece of state, exposes actions to update it, and notifies subscribers when it changes. Stores are framework-agnostic — they have no knowledge of React, Solid, or any UI library. Creating a store Use forge() to create one. Step 1 · Install Create a fresh app with whatever template you like. Then install Runeforge and the React adapter. # inside your app directory npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Step 2 · A counter store The smallest useful store has one piece of state and one action. Both are inferred from the object you pass to forge(). // stores/counter.ts import { forge } from "runeforge"; export const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { increment: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), decrement: (s) => ({ count: s.count - 1 }), reset: () => ({ count: 0 }), }, }); Use it in a component with useStore: // Counter.tsx import { useStore } from "@runeforge/react"; import { counter } from "./stores/counter"; export function Counter() { const count = useStore(counter, (s) => s.count); return (

{count}

); } Notice three things: No provider. The store is just an import — it's already global. The component subscribes to a selector (s.count), not the whole store. If another part of state changed, this component would not re-render. Actions are called like ordinary methods. There's no dispatch(). Step 3 · A todo list (and a derived store) For richer state, use a slice for todos and another for the filter. Then derive a third store that combines them. // stores/todos.ts import { forge, derive } from "runeforge"; export const todos = forge({ state: { items: [] as { id: number; text: string; done: boolean }[] }, actions: { add: (s, text: string) => ({ items: [...s.items, { id: Date.now(), text, done: false }] }), toggle: (s, id: number) => ({ items: s.items.map(t => t.id === id ? { ...t, done: !t.done } : t) }), remove: (s, id: number) => ({ items: s.items.filter(t => t.id !== id) }), clear: (s) => ({ items: s.items.filter(t => !t.done) }), }, }); export const filter = forge({ state: { mode: "all" as "all" | "active" | "done" }, actions: { setMode: (s, mode) => ({ mode }), }, }); // derive() runs only when its inputs change. export const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => { if (f.mode === "all") return t.items; if (f.mode === "active") return t.items.filter(x => !x.done); return t.items.filter(x => x.done); }); In the component, you subscribe to the derived store the same way you subscribe to a regular one: const visible = useStore(visibleTodos); return visible.map(t => ); Step 4 · Async (the easy way) Async work belongs in effects. Effects can read and write any store, await whatever they want, and report status into a status field. Runeforge ships an asyncSlice() helper that gives you a typed status object for free. import { forge, asyncSlice } from "runeforge"; export const users = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice() }, actions: { async load(s) { if (s.status === "loading") return s; try { const r = await fetch("/api/users"); const data = await r.json(); return { status: "ready", data, error: null }; } catch (e) { return { status: "error", data: null, error: e.message }; } }, }, }); Inside the component: const { status, data, err

observation.title: Runeforge — predictable state for JavaScript
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. RUNEFORGE REDUX TOOLKIT ZUSTAND JOTAI Bundle size (min+gz) 4.0 kB 13.6 kB 1.6 kB 3.9 kB Framework-agnostic Yes No (React-first) React-first React-only TypeScript inference Full Manual types Full Atom-by-atom Devtools Built-in (1 kB) External External External SSR / serialization First-class Manual Manual Manual Time-travel Yes Yes No No Next steps Build something in 5 minutes with the quickstart. Understand the model in Stores and Actions & selectors. Look up exact signatures in the API reference. See a working app in Examples. NEXT Quickstart → ON THIS PAGE Introduction Install Hello, store. observation.title: Stores — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Core concepts › Stores Core concept Stores. A store is the unit of state in Runeforge. It owns a single piece of state, exposes actions to update it, and notifies subscribers when it changes. Stores are framework-agnostic — they have no knowledge of React, Solid, or any UI library. Creating a store Use forge() to create one. The shape of the object you pass is the API of the store. import { forge } from "runeforge"; const session = forge({ state: { user: null as User | null, expiresAt: 0 }, actions: { login: (s, user: User, ttl: number) => ({ user, expiresAt: Date.now() + ttl }), logout: () => ({ user: null, expiresAt: 0 }), }, }); The returned store is a plain object with these methods, plus your actions as methods: MEMBER SIGNATURE DESCRIPTION get () => State Returns the current state (a frozen snapshot). set (next: Partial<State>) => void Imperative state update. Prefer actions in most cases. subscribe (listener) => unsubscribe Calls listener on every committed state change. select (selector) => SelectedView Returns a derived view that's its own subscribable store. reset () => void Returns to the initial state. Useful in tests. name string Auto-derived debug name, or passed via the options bag. Reading and subscribing The simplest store is read with get() and observed with subscribe(): const current = session.get(); // { user: null, expiresAt: 0 } const off = session.subscribe((next, prev) => { console.log("changed:", prev, "→", next); }); // later off(); State is immutable. Each commit replaces the previous state with a new frozen object. Don't try to mutate s.user.name = "x" — return a new object instead. Runeforge will warn in dev if it detects an in-place mutation. Composing stores Apps usually have several stores. They compose by importing each other and using derive(): import { derive } from "runeforge"; import { session } from "./session"; import { feed } from "./feed"; export const homepage = derive( [session, feed], (s, f) => ({ greeting: s.user ? `Welcome back, ${s.user.name}` : "Welcome", items: s.user ? f.items : f.items.slice(0, 5), }) ); derive only recomputes when one of its inputs changes — and only emits a notification when its output changes (by structural equality). It's the right tool for "computed views" or "memoized selectors". Slicing a store For very large stores, store.select() returns a slice that behaves like its own store: const currentUser = session.select((s) => s.user); currentUser.subscribe((u) => render(u)); // fires only when `s.user` changes — not on `expiresAt` changes Server-side rendering & serialization Every store can be serialized with store.toJSON() and rehydrated with store.fromJSON(). The intended flow on the server is: create stores, prime them with fetched data, render once, ship the dehydrated state along with the HTML. // server session.login(user, 3600_000); const html = renderToString(<App />); const state = { session: session.toJSON(), feed: feed.toJSON() }; // client session.fromJSON(state.session); feed.fromJSON(state.feed); hydrate(<App />); Testing stores Stores are easy to unit-test because they have no framework. Prefer actions in most cases. subscribe (listener) => unsubscribe Calls listener on every committed state change. select (selector) => SelectedView Returns a derived view that's its own subscribable store. reset () => void Returns to the initial state. Useful in tests. name string Auto-derived debug name, or passed via the options bag. observation.title: Actions & selectors — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools REFERENCE API reference Docs › Core concepts › Actions & selectors Core concept Actions & selectors. Actions describe how state changes. Selectors describe how state is read. Together they give you a one-way data flow without the ceremony of Redux. Actions An action is a function on a store. It receives the current state and any arguments you pass, and returns the next state — or a partial of it. const cart = forge({ state: { items: [] as Item[], coupon: null as string | null }, actions: { add: (s, item: Item) => ({ items: [...s.items, item] }), remove: (s, id: number) => ({ items: s.items.filter(i => i.id !== id) }), apply: (s, code: string) => ({ coupon: code }), clear: () => ({ items: [], coupon: null }), }, }); // call them like methods cart.add({ id: 1, name: "Espresso", price: 3.50 }); cart.apply("BLOOM10"); Rules of thumb Return, don't mutate. Always return a new object. Spread, map, filter — but never assign in place. Return a partial. The partial is shallow-merged with current state, so you only return what changed. Stay synchronous if possible. Keep async work in effects (see the Async & effects guide). It makes actions trivially testable. Name actions for what they do, not how they do it. checkout() is better than setCheckoutState(true). Selectors A selector is a pure function from state to a derived value. Components — and any subscriber, really — use selectors so they only re-render when the value they care about changes. const totalPrice = (s: ReturnType<typeof cart.get>) => s.items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price, 0); cart.subscribe((s) => render(totalPrice(s))); // fires every change cart.select(totalPrice).subscribe(render); // fires only when total actually changes Composing selectors Selectors compose like any other pure functions. For more involved derivations across multiple stores, prefer derive() — it caches and only recomputes when its inputs change. import { derive } from "runeforge"; import { cart, coupons } from "./stores"; export const grandTotal = derive([cart, coupons], (c, cs) => { const sub = c.items.reduce((s, i) => s + i.price, 0); const off = c.coupon ? cs.discountFor(c.coupon) : 0; return { sub, discount: off, total: Math.max(0, sub - off) }; }); Reusable action creators For common patterns, Runeforge ships builder helpers like asyncSlice(), listSlice(), and formSlice(). They generate action sets so you don't write the same CRUD by hand. import { forge, listSlice } from "runeforge"; type Todo = { id: number; text: string; done: boolean }; export const todos = forge({ state: listSlice<Todo>().state, actions: listSlice<Todo>().actions("id"), }); // generated: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count todos.add({ id: 1, text: "Write docs", done: false }); todos.update(1, (t) => ({ done: true })); Action middleware Middleware wraps actions. Use it for logging, time-travel, persistence, and analytics. Middleware are pure functions that run before and after every commit. import { use } from "runeforge"; use((next) => (action, args) => { const t0 = performance.now(); const r = next(action, args); console.log(`${action.store}.${action.name}`, `${(performance.now() - t0).toFixed(1)}ms`); return r; }); The order is the order you call use() in. Devtools, persistence, and time-travel are all middleware — and you can write your own with the same signature. observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

observation.title: Runeforge — predictable state for JavaScript
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. RUNEFORGE REDUX TOOLKIT ZUSTAND JOTAI Bundle size (min+gz) 4.0 kB 13.6 kB 1.6 kB 3.9 kB Framework-agnostic Yes No (React-first) React-first React-only TypeScript inference Full Manual types Full Atom-by-atom Devtools Built-in (1 kB) External External External SSR / serialization First-class Manual Manual Manual Time-travel Yes Yes No No Next steps Build something in 5 minutes with the quickstart. Understand the model in Stores and Actions & selectors. Look up exact signatures in the API reference. See a working app in Examples. NEXT Quickstart → ON THIS PAGE Introduction Install Hello, store. observation.title: Runeforge — predictable state for JavaScript
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. RUNEFORGE REDUX TOOLKIT ZUSTAND JOTAI Bundle size (min+gz) 4.0 kB 13.6 kB 1.6 kB 3.9 kB Framework-agnostic Yes No (React-first) React-first React-only TypeScript inference Full Manual types Full Atom-by-atom Devtools Built-in (1 kB) External External External SSR / serialization First-class Manual Manual Manual Time-travel Yes Yes No No Next steps Build something in 5 minutes with the quickstart. Understand the model in Stores and Actions & selectors. Look up exact signatures in the API reference. See a working app in Examples. NEXT Quickstart → ON THIS PAGE Introduction Install Hello, store. Three things to remember Why another state library? Next steps Edit this page on GitHub → Discuss on the forum

observation.title: Examples — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) ☾ ★ 18.4k Docs › Examples Examples Apps you can fork. Self-contained example apps. Every one of them is under 500 lines and uses just the public API. Clone the repo, npm i, npm dev — that's the whole setup. All (12) Beginner Intermediate Advanced SSR beginner Counter (the canonical hello-world) The smallest possible Runeforge app. Single store, three actions, one component. React 34 LOC beginner Todo list with persistence Add / toggle / delete todos. State persists to localStorage with one option. React 88 LOC beginner Async fetcher with retry asyncSlice() pattern. Loads users with exponential-backoff retry on failure. Vue 3 110 LOC intermediate Multi-step form (typed) Uses formSlice() to manage values, errors, touched state, and submission. React 210 LOC intermediate Optimistic comments Show comments instantly, roll back on server error. Uses derive() + middleware. Solid 180 LOC intermediate Realtime presence WebSocket push updates per-user presence and merges into store. Svelte 5 240 LOC intermediate Routing-aware state Read URL params into a store; navigation is just an action. React 160 LOC advanced Undo / redo with snapshots Time-travel using built-in snapshot support. Cmd-Z / Cmd-Shift-Z. React 320 LOC advanced Server-side rendered shop Full SSR + hydration of multiple stores. Includes server-only state. React (Next 15) 460 LOC advanced Markdown editor with autosave Debounced autosave middleware, file-system adapter, and conflict detection. Vanilla JS 420 LOC advanced Spreadsheet with cross-cell formulas Each cell is a derived store; recompute graph triggered by edits. Solid 480 LOC advanced Drag-and-drop kanban (SSR) Move cards between columns; renders identically on server and client. React (Next 15) 440 LOC

observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. RUNEFORGE REDUX TOOLKIT ZUSTAND JOTAI Bundle size (min+gz) 4.0 kB 13.6 kB 1.6 kB 3.9 kB Framework-agnostic Yes No (React-first) React-first React-only TypeScript inference Full Manual types Full Atom-by-atom Devtools Built-in (1 kB) External External External SSR / serialization First-class Manual Manual Manual Time-travel Yes Yes No No Next steps Build something in 5 minutes with the quickstart. observation.title: Runeforge — predictable state for JavaScript
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. RUNEFORGE REDUX TOOLKIT ZUSTAND JOTAI Bundle size (min+gz) 4.0 kB 13.6 kB 1.6 kB 3.9 kB Framework-agnostic Yes No (React-first) React-first React-only TypeScript inference Full Manual types Full Atom-by-atom Devtools Built-in (1 kB) External External External SSR / serialization First-class Manual Manual Manual Time-travel Yes Yes No No Next steps Build something in 5 minutes with the quickstart. Understand the model in Stores and Actions & selectors. Look up exact signatures in the API reference. See a working app in Examples. NEXT Quickstart → ON THIS PAGE Introduction Install Hello, store. Three things to remember Why another state library? observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

observation.title: Runeforge — predictable state for JavaScript
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. RUNEFORGE REDUX TOOLKIT ZUSTAND JOTAI Bundle size (min+gz) 4.0 kB 13.6 kB 1.6 kB 3.9 kB Framework-agnostic Yes No (React-first) React-first React-only TypeScript inference Full Manual types Full Atom-by-atom Devtools Built-in (1 kB) External External External SSR / serialization First-class Manual Manual Manual Time-travel Yes Yes No No Next steps Build something in 5 minutes with the quickstart. Understand the model in Stores and Actions & selectors. Look up exact signatures in the API reference. See a working app in Examples. NEXT Quickstart → ON THIS PAGE Introduction Install Hello, store. observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level.
